context:
Goal: main stays green and the records page stays current.
Problem (rule): a merge made with GitHub's button, or by auto-merge, skips the merge tool's records rebuild, so the page goes stale and main's check turns red. Which fix fits turns on one fact only you know: how often you press that button yourself.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/no-merge-during-batch-ci.md lines 33-35.
Based on (read): lane notes-keep-reverify, 14:48 CST: a stops Claude causing the gap but not your own presses; b covers every merge but costs an extra PR and CI run per merge.
Departs from: main, where a button merge can leave the page stale. a adds one guard rule; b adds a rebuild PR after each merge.

options.gain: One small guard rule; Claude can no longer cause a stale page.
options.label: Rarely or never: a hook refuses auto-merge for Claude, and the button stays yours (recommended)
options.lose: If you do press the button, the page can still go stale until the next merge-tool merge rebuilds it.

options.gain: Every merge path keeps the page current, your presses included.
options.label: Often: after any merge, a bot opens a rebuild PR that the batch runner merges
options.lose: One extra PR and CI run per merge, and more work to build.

reply: 19:12 CST: a (you rarely press the button: a hook refuses auto-merge for Claude, and the button stays yours). Home: roadmap step auto-merge-refused-for-claude, routed to the coordinator; decision no-merge-during-batch-ci records it when the lane lands.
short: Do you press GitHub's merge button often?
title: Do you often merge pull requests with GitHub's merge button yourself?
why: Lane notes-keep-reverify, from kept note merge-by-button-stale-page.
